children: Gaming groups Lottomatica and Cirsa Enterprises have agreed to an all-share merger deal that will see the combined entity retain a listing in both Italy and Spain.

Milan-listed Lottomatica said that Wednesday's deal will see shareholders of Barcelona-based Cirsa receive 0.668 newly issued Lottomatica shares for each share held, with current Lottomatica shareholders expected to own 67.5% of the combined company and Cirsa shareholders holding the remaining 32.5%.
Lottomatica will continue as the surviving entity, with the new group retaining the Lottomatica name.

"The proposed combination will create a global leading sports betting and gaming player, with number one positions in Italy and Spain, and leading presence in other high-growth markets," the companies said in a joint statement.

They said the deal will create the second-largest listed gaming and sports betting operator globally, with pro forma adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization of around 2 billion euros ($2.32 billion) in the year to June 30.

The companies also said that the combined group will have online growth opportunities, yield around 115 million euros of pretax cash annual synergies, and greater capacity for dividends and buybacks with up to 4 billion euros of capital returns expected over the next three years.

Cirsa's majority shareholder, LHMC Midco, a company controlled by Blackstone, has also agreed to the deal, with Blackstone expected to become the largest shareholder of the combined company with a 24% stake. It will be represented on the board by two directors.

"We see a compelling opportunity to build on the strengths of both organisations, creating a stronger and more diversified platform with greater scale and enhanced capabilities to accelerate growth and value creation," said Laurence Van Lancker, Lottomatica's deputy chief executive and chief financial officer.
Van Lancker will retain his position in the combined group, as will Lottomatica Chief Executive Guglielmo Angelozzi.

Before implementing the merger, Cirsa will distribute to its shareholders an extraordinary dividend of 262 million euros, or 1.56 euros per share. Upon completion, Lottomatica intends to propose shareholders of the combined company a capital return of 744 million euros.
The proposed merger is expected to close in the second quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.
